summary:
Project developed as part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge Calumbo 2026
A municipal and community decision-support system for mitigating the impacts of drought and managing rangelands in Southern Angola, utilizing Earth observation data from NASA.
details:
Millions of families in southern Angola—notably in Cunene province and adjacent areas—rely on agriculture and livestock farming. Currently, the impacts of drought are often identified only once severe crop losses or livestock mortality have already occurred.

This solution translates raw data from NASA satellites into an intuitive Situation Room, enabling municipal administrations, rural authorities, and cooperatives to identify water stress in vegetation weeks in advance and guide the preemptive relocation of livestock.
